title: Generate Parentheses Problem

notes: Return all distinct well-formed parentheses strings that use exactly n pairs.
For n = 0, return [""] because the empty string is the unique balanced sequence with zero pairs.
Only strings with exactly n opening and n closing parentheses are valid outputs.
The judge compares outputs as sets, so returned order does not matter.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [n]. Example: [3]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialised list of strings (order does not matter). Example: ["((()))","(()())","(())()","()(())","()()()"]

sampleTestCases.explanation: There are 5 valid combinations for three pairs.
There is exactly one valid combination for one pair.

content.problemStatement:
You receive `n` pairs of parentheses. Generate all combinations of well-formed (balanced) parentheses using exactly `n` pairs. Output the list of distinct valid strings. The order of strings in the returned list does not matter.

A string of parentheses is well-formed if every opening parenthesis has a matching closing parenthesis and pairs are properly nested. As an example, for `n = 3` the valid combinations are `"((()))","(()())","(())()","()(())","()()()"`.

Aim for an algorithm that runs in time proportional to the number of valid combinations (Catalan number) and uses O(n) auxiliary space for recursion/stack (excluding the output list).

notes: Output order does not matter; the judge should compare the returned set of strings.
Generator cases are deterministic and use JavaScript only.
The invariant closeCount <= openCount ensures every generated prefix can still become well-formed.
Every valid combination is generated exactly once.
With n <= 8, the maximum output count is Catalan(8) = 1430.
solution.approach: Backtracking: build the sequence one character at a time while tracking the number of opening and closing parentheses already used. Add '(' only while fewer than n opening parentheses have been used. Add ')' only when it will not make closing parentheses exceed opening parentheses. When length 2*n is reached, add the valid sequence to the result.

better.complexity: Exponential time with unnecessary invalid branches and O(n) auxiliary space.
better.description: Use recursive generation but still allow arbitrary prefixes, then validate completed strings. This reduces some overhead compared with full enumeration but still explores many invalid prefixes.

optimal.complexity: O(Catalan(n) * n) time and O(n) auxiliary space excluding output.
optimal.description: Use constrained backtracking. Open a new pair whenever openCount < n. Add a closing parenthesis only when closeCount < openCount. This prunes every invalid prefix before it is generated.

bruteForce.complexity: O(4^n * n) time and O(n) auxiliary space excluding output.
bruteForce.description: Generate all 2^(2n) strings of '(' and ')' of length 2n and filter out invalid strings. This produces a large number of candidates that can never be valid.

solution.timeComplexity: O(Catalan(n) * n), where Catalan(n) is the number of valid output strings.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary recursion and construction space, excluding the output list.

followUps: Can you implement the same generation iteratively with an explicit stack?
How does the Catalan number explain the output size?
What changes if n is increased beyond 8?
learningObjectives: Relate enumeration problems to Catalan numbers.
